title: ANDS Studio overall product concept
walkthrough:
You land — once signed in (the app redirects any signed-out visitor to a login page first) — on a page with a slim top bar reading "ANDS Studio" and, in small text, "· file a drug like a story". The hero headline says "File a drug with Health Canada, like telling a story." A paragraph explains that an Abbreviated New Drug Submission is complex and that the tool walks you through it step by step, "showing your submission take shape in 3D until it's ready to send. No regulatory background needed." Below sits one primary button, "Start my submission →", a secondary link "Or open your dossiers — every product in submission →", and a footnote: "Grounded in real Health Canada process · your progress is saved automatically".

Clicking start opens a three-panel layout. A left rail titled "Your filing journey" lists eleven steps in order: "Get oriented", "Set up your company", "Get your product's file number", "Start a submission", "Add your documents", "Check your submission", "Pay the fees", "Get it approved", "Sign", "Submit to Health Canada", "Track & respond". The current step is marked "You're here"; completed ones say "Done"; later steps show a lock icon with a plain-language reason (e.g. "Complete "Set up your company" first."). The center panel holds the active step's card; a right column shows a 3D stack of module tiles ("Your submission · Module 1–5") plus a readiness card whose blockers spell out each unlock requirement (e.g. "A Company ID exists"). The top bar adds a status chip — "Ready to file" or e.g. "40% ready" — and a "Start over" button.

Choosing "My dossiers" opens the dossier manager ("ANDS Studio · dossier manager"), with nav chips "Portfolio", "Registry", "Correspondence", "Guided journey →". Under the heading "Your product dossiers", a note explains a Dossier ID "is the permanent file for one product at Health Canada." If none exist: "No dossiers yet. Create one to start building a submission." Clicking "New dossier +" reveals two fields, "Dossier ID" (placeholder "e123456") and "Product name" (placeholder "Drugazole 10 mg tablet"), and "Create & open →". You must already know your Dossier ID and its format — a wrong entry returns "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)". Each dossier tile shows the ID, title, a progress bar, a chip like "Ready to file" or "3/5 modules", and a ✕ delete that asks for confirmation ("This cannot be undone.").

Opening a dossier lands in a module workspace: tabs "M1" through "M5" (check, dash, or dot marking each module's state), chips "Application Viewer", "Audit", "Portfolio", "Journey". A left tree lists eCTD sections; the center panel explains "What Health Canada needs here" and offers tabs "⬆ Upload", "✦ Author in-app", and "⊘ Mark N/A", with a "Drop a file" zone. The right column repeats the tower and a counter of required sections complete.
